chapter: Hurry On Down, Capitol and New York
title: Carlos Gastel as manager
summary: She and Willard recall Gastel's loud shirts and warmth and how he got her recognition and good pay.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: And Carlos handled everything for you?
Yes, he handled all of that.
When I think of him I always think of him going to elegant opening nights in those loud, loud colored sports shirts.
And loafer shoes, and no tie and no jacket. And it didn't matter what --
-- how elegant a place it was or what their code was, nobody ever dreamed of turning down Carlos Gastel.
And he never dreamed of dressing like anybody else.
No, not like anybody else. But he was
a very warm, personable man, and --

Everybody loved him, because he loved everybody. He loved people, you know, he was just that type of person. And -- well, I really considered myself lucky to be handled by somebody like him, you know.
He took good care of his artists.

Because he would see to it that you got recognition. That's one thing you did get, you know. And he didn't go for any peanuts, you know, he didn't go for that. So I was very fortunate, and I was very grateful to Mr. Dexter, because I'm sure Carlos Gastell didn't have to have Nellie Lutcher at that time, because he had Nat Cole and all these other people that I just mentioned, so he surely didn't need Nellie Lutcher.
